title: Josh Inglis Makes Australian History With Comeback Test Century in Cape Town Decider
excerpt: Recalled at short notice after a finger injury, Inglis scored 102 off 135 balls against South Africa at Newlands to become the first Australian with multiple centuries in all three international formats.
body:
• Josh Inglis scored 102 off 135 balls in the third Test against South Africa at Newlands, reaching his hundred off 132 deliveries with a reverse sweep.
  • He is the first Australian to score multiple centuries in all three international formats — Tests, ODIs and T20Is.
  • Inglis was a late recall after Steve Smith was ruled out with a neck injury, and had been recovering from a fractured finger; he had not played a Test in almost a year.
  • His stand with Alex Carey (80) took Australia from 191/4 past South Africa's 329; Australia were 411/8 at lunch on day three, leading by 82.

Josh Inglis etched his name into Australian cricket history on Thursday, scoring a comeback century in the series-deciding third Test against South Africa at Newlands to become the first Australian with multiple centuries across all three formats of the game.

Inglis, recalled to the Test XI after nearly a year out, made 102 off 135 balls with 11 fours and two sixes. He reached his hundred off 132 balls with a reverse sweep off Simon Harmer on the third morning, before edging the same bowler behind to wicketkeeper Ryan Rickelton in the same over, according to Fox Sports' live coverage.

A record nobody else holds

This was Inglis's second Test century — his first came on debut against Sri Lanka in Galle last year, when he made 102 off just 90 balls, the second-fastest hundred by a batter on Test debut. The Cape Town ton completes a set no Australian has managed: multiple centuries in Tests, ODIs and T20Is. Glenn Maxwell has five T20I hundreds and four ODI hundreds but only one Test century, against India in 2017. Aaron Finch scored two T20I hundreds and 17 ODI hundreds but never a Test hundred. Inglis now has at least two in each format.

Thirty minutes' notice

The innings was unlikely on several levels. Inglis was drafted in at short notice — reportedly about 30 minutes before the match — after Steve Smith was ruled out with a neck injury. He had been recovering from a fractured finger sustained during the preceding ODI series against South Africa, had missed the first two Tests, and had not played competitive red-ball cricket since March. Australia made four changes for the decider, with Cameron Green, Nathan Lyon and Cooper Connolly also returning.

Walking in with Australia in difficulty after Marco Jansen removed Green and Labuschagne in quick succession, Inglis counter-attacked alongside Alex Carey, who made 80. Their partnership carried Australia past South Africa's first-innings 329, and by lunch on day three the visitors were 411 for 8, a lead of 82, with Connolly and Lyon at the crease — the match, and the series, still live.

The IPL connection

Indian audiences have their own reference point for Inglis: he was Punjab Kings' Rs 2.60 crore signing for IPL 2025, and Lucknow Super Giants paid Rs 8.6 crore for him at the IPL 2026 mini-auction despite his signalling limited availability that season. A wicketkeeper-batter who can score a 132-ball Test hundred on recall, in a decider away from home, explains why franchises keep paying for the option.
